points.description: States that the * operator returns an alias/synonym (or reference/lvalue name) for the object that its operand points to in memory. Equivalent wording such as 'a reference to the pointed-to object' earns full marks. Merely saying it returns the value stored at the address is only partial.
points.partial_credit: Half credit for saying it accesses/returns the value stored at the pointed-to address without saying it is an alias/synonym/reference to the object itself.

levels.says: Says the operator returns or accesses the value stored at the address the operand points to, but does not say it is an alias/synonym/reference to the object itself.

points.description: Identifies the * operator as the dereferencing operator. Accept 'dereference operator', 'indirection operator', or equivalent wording.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the idea that * gives an alias/synonym/reference to the pointed-to object and the name 'dereferencing operator'. A partly correct answer that only says it gets the value stored at the address earns half credit on P1 but not P2. Answers saying it returns an address/pointer, or describing multiplication, earn no marks.
